result_notes.M::thm:main: Over C, all finite-dimensional V including dimension zero and all integer b>=6: SOME GL(V)-equivariant injection Sym^6(Sym^b V) -> Sym^b(Sym^6 V). Equivalent stable Schur positivity, not injectivity of the specified canonical Psi_6,b. Diagonal b=6 uses identity representation, canonical Psi_6,6 can have a kernel. Two alternative large-degree proof routes; neither local C++ recomputation nor complete formal/human proof audit performed.
result_notes.M::cor:quadratic-range: At a=6 the companion canonical MULTIPLICATION mu_6,b=Psi_b,6 is surjective for b>=30; complete reducibility supplies a section and hence a representation embedding. Direction is reversed from Psi_6,b. This route reduces needed nontrivial finite b to7..29; independent chart route remains separately available.
result_notes.M::lem:rectangles: In six gap coordinates d_i=lambda_i-lambda_(i+1), lambda_7=0, target Q(d+6e_i)>=Q(d) for each i. Multiply by ONE nonzero highest-weight vector in a domain, not product of multiplicities. Source F(d+6e_6)=F(d) since determinant^6 is trivial on permutation S6. For b>=26,d6>=6, reduce b by6 leaving>=20.
result_notes.M::lem:chart: For a>=2, finite V and f in equal-row degree k invariant R_k, z(v)^L f lies in A_(k+L) if k+L>=a k, where A is generated by R_1 and z(v)=v tensor a. Local chart requires nonzero v, and ratio invariant of total degree t uses <=t polarized elementary factors. Cancellation in a polynomial domain; no numeric condition estimate.
result_notes.M::cor:first-row: For lambda of6b with tail t1=lambda2+...+lambda6<=b, the full lambda highest-weight space of R_b is in A_b; hence coefficient comparison. This is an exact invariant-space argument, not empirical finite-grid observation.
result_notes.M::lem:polarization: For L>=1 and j>=a L, W_j is spanned by z(v)^L W_(j-L) over all v; averaging yields the R analogue. Iterated directional derivatives use strictly positive source-minus-destination degree at every shift. Field C and polarization factorials matter.
result_notes.M::cor:module-generation: Equal-row invariant ring R is generated as A-module by pieces of degrees0..a-1, using L=1 polarization. Finite module generation does not make all low-degree pieces already generated by R_1 or compute least stabilization.
result_notes.M::prop:large: Independent chart and polarization route, without companion quadratic theorem: R_b=A_b for a>=2,b>=a(a-1)^2, hence representation embedding; at a=6 threshold150. Combined with FULL finite b6..149 certificates supplies an alternative proof route. No runtime/rank-conditioning statement.
result_notes.M::lem:strips: For |gamma|-|mu|=i b, coefficient [s_gamma] h_b(X^i)s_mu belongs to{0,+1,-1}. Nonzero requires gamma_j>=mu_j>=gamma_(j+i) and residue matching; determinant sorting determines sign. Do not drop signs or transfer to arbitrary plethysm coefficients.
result_notes.M::prop:upper: U(d) bounds F(d) via cycle formula on S6 and gap-width products for equal-weight Kostka counts, minimizing over removal orders; U is coordinatewise monotone on all nonnegative gaps even inadmissible weight. Discarding cycle signs/constraints gives upper bound, not exact source multiplicity.
result_notes.M::lem:sumset: Old Matolcsi-Ruzsa-type lower bound for finite D with C elements and affine real dimension h: |kD|>=binom(k+h,h)+(C-1-h)binom(k+h-1,h). Triangulation includes every point, and half-open assignments avoid double counts. This lemma is not a new F210 application improvement.
result_notes.M::prop:power: From Q(x)>=C>0 with positive degree d0=w(x)/6, choose z=min(18,min{h:binom(d0+h,h)>=C}); Q(kx)>=f(C,z,k). Row-reduced distinct leading monomials give C exponent vectors on degree d0 hyperplane and affine dimension>=z; distinct SUMS certify independent products. Does not assert C^k independent products. Cap18 weakens a lower bound.

result_notes.Q::thm:main: For finite-dimensional complex V including zero,a>=2,b>=a(a-1), normalized canonical mu:Sym^b(Sym^a V)->Sym^a(Sym^b V) is SURJECTIVE. Equivalent A_b=R_b. Sufficient quadratic threshold, not least/sharp threshold, and not injectivity of the reverse canonical map. a=1 is separately bijective.
result_notes.Q::lem:shift: With any finite independent spectator variables, D_Y/U=sum Y_i partial_Ui is injective on bihomogeneous (p,q) piece if p>q. Fischer monomial norm alpha!, adjoint E, ED-DE=N_U-N_Y gives norm(Dh)^2-norm(Eh)^2=(p-q)norm(h)^2. Main paper complex proof; selected Lean algebraic analogue additionally needs sl2 commutators and opposite local nilpotence over CharZero, not arbitrary operators.
result_notes.Q::prop:vanishing: Symmetric a-linear form T on Sym^b V whose diagonal vanishes on every product of b vectors is zero under b>=a(a-1),a>=1,b>=1. Induct r=a-1,m=b-r>=r^2; binary X^r+cY^r splitting, first m distinct directional shifts with positive weights, induction on r, then r^2 common-destination shifts. Product inputs may repeat or be zero; does not test merely finitely many samples.
result_notes.Q::cor:comparison: There EXISTS a GL(V)-equivariant injection in reverse direction under same complex finite-dimensional/quadratic hypotheses. Natural proof uses invariant complement; actual selected Lean uses perfect pairings and surjection at V dual. Neither proves that arbitrary computational choice of inverse is equivariant nor a fast/noise-stable section.
